image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on rippled water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a chestnut-brown chest, and a greyish-white body. It has a bright yellow bill and is positioned in profile facing left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and bright yellow, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible as a small, dark spot on the green head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing streamlined and buoyant on the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing typical feather layering and shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, appearing short and slightly upturned, consistent with drake anatomy.
